Digi Power X Inc. Q3 2026 Earnings Call Summary - Moby
Strategic Pivot to AI Infrastructure

Our analysts just identified a stock with the potential to be the next Nvidia. Tell us how you invest and we'll show you why it's our #1 pick. Tap here.

Revenue increased 85% sequentially as the company successfully transitioned from a legacy Bitcoin mining operation to an AI infrastructure provider, with AI now representing 46% of total revenue.

The launch of the NeoCloudz Token Factory in Berlin allows the company to capture 85%-90% margins by selling AI inference directly to customers rather than renting compute at wholesale prices.

Management attributes the rapid seven-month execution of the Columbiana Phase I facility to a 'full-stack' ownership model that controls everything from power generation to data center design.

Strategic financial discipline is being maintained by prioritizing project-level debt and customer prepayments over equity issuance to minimize shareholder dilution during rapid expansion.

The decision to keep US Data Centers Inc. as a separate capital-raising entity allows the company to participate in modular AI and robotics growth without diverting core capital from infrastructure projects.

Operational efficiency improved significantly during the quarter, with management reducing SG&A expenses by 30% compared to the previous quarter through a disciplined entrepreneurial approach.

2027 Growth and Capacity Outlook

Management targets an annualized revenue run rate of $250 million to $300 million by the end of Q3 2027, supported by existing contracts and pending customer negotiations.

Phase I of the Columbiana AI campus is on schedule for tenant access on December 15, 2026, with contractual billing expected to commence in January 2027.

The 2027 capital plan of approximately $350 million will focus on completing Columbiana Phase II and expanding AI inference capacity to 10 MW.

Long-term expansion plans include converting New York power assets to AI data centers in late 2027 and developing 150 MW of capacity in North Carolina by 2030.

The company expects to close a $200 million project-level debt facility syndicated by Goldman Sachs in Q4 2026 to fund the completion of the 40 MW Columbiana project.

Contractual and Structural Highlights

The 10-year take-or-pay agreement with Cerebras carries a total potential contract value of approximately $2.5 billion if all extension options are exercised.

Management successfully renegotiated debt financing terms through Goldman Sachs, achieving single-digit interest rates and saving approximately 2 points compared to previous offers.

The company holds approximately $119.6 million in cash, equivalents, and digital currencies, providing a foundation for the next phase of infrastructure deployment.

Q&A Strategic Insights
Funding strategy for the $350 million 2027 capital plan

Management is leveraging its execution credibility to secure significantly higher customer deposits, ranging from 30% to 70% on new contracts.

This 'customer-funded' model is designed to finance growth while avoiding the equity market volatility that has impacted the stock price.

Sustainability of high margins in the NeoCloudz sector

The 85%-90% margins are sustainable because the company owns the power generation and the full technology stack, capturing the value of every token served.

Management views power as the primary bottleneck in the industry, making their permitted, connected power assets increasingly valuable for high-margin inference.

Valuation of completed liquid-cooled AI data center assets

Management estimates the market value of finished liquid-cooled data centers at $30 million to $35 million per megawatt based on recent industry transactions.

Applying this to the 40 MW Columbiana project suggests a potential net equity value of approximately $1.2 billion upon completion.

Strategic rationale for the US Data Centers Inc. structure

The 48% ownership allows Digi Power X to benefit from modular AI and robotics innovation without the risk of allocating core capital to new ventures.

USDC is raising capital independently to avoid diluting Digi Power X shareholders while developing automated deployment systems for 2027-2028.

Stability of the Cerebras partnership following market volatility

Management expressed high confidence in Cerebras, noting their strong cash position and 55% year-over-year growth as a key alternative to NVIDIA.

The relationship is bolstered by the high switching costs for tenants in specialized liquid-cooled facilities and the scarcity of available power shells.

title: Better Chip Stock: Nvidia vs. AMD
detail:
Better Chip Stock: Nvidia vs. AMD

Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) shareholders have had a rough few days. After a week in which news broke that CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang had engaged in an extramarital affair with a woman who is accused of being a Chinese spy, and another with an Nvidia executive, on Thursday morning, he resigned.

The exit of the man who has been the face of the company for decades has investors worried about its future. AMD (NASDAQ:AMD) shareholders aren't in the same boat, and the chipmaker is enjoying surging data center sales.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

However, the question remains: Which stock is the better buy? It's a hard question to answer, because at face value, Nvidia is doing far better than AMD. But AMD doesn't have other questions surrounding the state of its business.

What matters is what you value most as an investor, as Nvidia is likely to be a tumultuous stock to own over the next few months.

Image source: Getty Images.

Nvidia is still winning the AI processor race

Before comparing Nvidia and AMD stocks, investors must answer a different question: How capable will Nvidia be without Huang in the CEO role? If you're of the view that the company's future really rests on the caliber of the person in the top job, then Nvidia's investment thesis can't be properly analyzed until his permanent successor is picked. For now, respected CFO Colette Kress occupies the role on an interim basis.

If it doesn't matter to you who is leading Nvidia, then you're free to proceed to the next point.

Nvidia and AMD are both computing unit designers, although their businesses look a bit different. AMD's product lineup is a lot broader than Nvidia's, and so is its customer base. It has sizable businesses in the consumer electronics world as well as in embedded processors and data centers. However, almost all investors care about is the data center business, as that's what is growing rapidly right now.

During Q3, AMD's data center revenue rose 97% year over year to $8.5 billion. That's a strong result, and investors are excited. However, because AMD also has fairly large exposure to other segments, its overall growth rate was 45%, bringing its top line to $13.4 billion. The problem is it isn't anywhere close to Nvidia's growth and size.

Nvidia reports its fiscal 2027 Q3 results on Nov. 17. But until we get that update about the recent state of the business, the best we can do is to use its fiscal Q2 results. In that period, its data center sales rose 117% year over year to $89 billion. Because Nvidia's data center business makes up a far larger chunk of its total, Nvidia's overall revenue growth rate was 106% to $96.2 billion.

Nothing that has transpired over the past week will affect what Nvidia reports in Q3, and I'd expect another quarter of outperforming AMD based on historical trends. Furthermore, Nvidia has already told investors to expect 70% revenue growth in its fiscal 2028. Management is comfortable giving that guidance because Nvidia's business is practically locked in, with AI hyperscalers ordering its processors far in advance of when they'll be ready to install them in data centers.

I think this supports the premise that Nvidia can keep succeeding without Huang as CEO, because it's already got a lot of future growth on the books due to how strong a business it has built.

So, from a growth standpoint, Nvidia is still the better pick. And after this month's sell-off, the stock is even cheaper.

AMD's stock is pricey

The best way to weigh the value of these two stocks is to look at their expected earnings for next year. By that metric, AMD is about 3 times more expensive than Nvidia.

NVDA PE Ratio (Forward 1y) data by YCharts

That seems like a huge premium to pay for AMD, and the reality is that regardless of who is running Nvidia, a pricing mismatch of that magnitude is too great to ignore. Nvidia's stock could triple from this point without looking too expensive, and even a double would leave the stock looking cheap compared to its growth rate.

I think Nvidia is the far better stock to buy here, mainly due to how cheap the stock is. Nvidia's business is strong, and its board should find a talented new leader to take it over.
